spans.s:
1. हित्वा, ind. (for 2. see p. 1171, col. 1), having
left or abandoned, having quitted or renounced, hav-
ing deserted; letting alone, slighting, disregarding.

2. हित्वा, ind. (for 1. see p. 1170, col. 1), having
sent; having impelled; having gone.

3. हित्वा, ind. (for 2. see p. 1171, col. 1), having
put or placed, having made, &c.

हित्वाय, ind., Ved. having abandoned, having
left, having discarded, (Sāy. = हित्वा = परित्यज्य,
Ṛg-veda

1. हित, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see p. 1172), sent,
impelled; gone, proceeded.

हित 2. हित, अस्, आ, अम् (past pass. part. of
rt. 1. धा; for 1. हित see under rt. 2. हि, p. 1171),
put, placed, laid, imposed [cf. 1. धित]; held, taken,
seized; suitable, proper, fit, worthy, right, advan-
tageous, beneficial, profitable, useful, salutary, whole-
some, agreeing with (often said in a medical sense
of diet, regimen, medicines, &c.); friendly, affec-
tionate, kind, (in these senses hardly distinguishable
fr. 1. हित); (अस्), m. a friend, benefactor; benefit,
profit, service, good, welfare, well-being; (आ), f. a
causeway, dike; (अम्), n. anything suitable or proper,
an advantage.
—हित-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, doing what
is fit or proper, doing a service, performing a kind-
ness, befriending, friendly, favourable; (अस्), m. a
benefactor.
—हित-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing well
to, desirous of benefiting or befriending.
—हित-
काम्या, f. desire for another's welfare, good-will.
—हित-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, or हित-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, doing
services, performing kindnesses or benefits, befriend-
ing, useful, beneficial, auspicious.
—हित-प्रणी, ईस्,
m. ‘executing what is advantageous,’ a spy, secret
emissary.
—हित-प्रयस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. one who
has offered an oblation of food, &c.
—हित-प्रेप्सु,
उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of effecting another's welfare,
wishing to benefit or befriend.
—हित-बुद्धि, इस्,
इस्, इ, friendly-minded, well-disposed, wishing well.
—हित-मित्र, अस्, m., Ved. a benevolent friend.
—हित-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, friendly, favourable, doing
good, useful.
—हित-वाक्य, अम्, n. friendly advice,
good counsel.
—हित-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, speaking
kindly, giving good counsel or friendly advice; (ई),
m. a friendly counsellor or adviser.
—हित-हरि-
वंश-गोस्वामिन्, ई, m. = हरि-वंश-गोस्वामिन्.
—हितानुकारिन् (˚त-अन्˚), ई, इणी, इ, acting con-
formably to what is right or kind.
—हितानुबन्-
धिन् (˚त-अन्˚), ई, इनी, इ, having welfare as a con-
sequence, involving or bringing welfare.
—हितान्-
वेषिन् (˚त-अन्˚), ई, इणी, इ, seeking another's wel-
fare.
—हिता-भङ्ग, अस्, m. the forcing or breaking
of a dike or causeway, (Manu

.)
—हितार्-
थिन् (˚त-अर्˚), ई, इनी, इ, seeking or desiring another's
welfare or advantage.
—हितावली (˚त-आव्˚), f. a
particular plant (= अङ्गार-कुष्ठक).
—हिताहित
(˚त-अह्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, good and evil, beneficial and
disadvantageous.
—हितेच्छा (˚त-इच्˚), f. well-wish-
ing, good-will, good wishes.
—हितैषिन् (˚त-एष्˚),
ई, इणी, इ, wishing well, desiring another's welfare,
kindly disposed, benevolent.
—हितोक्ति (˚त-उक्˚), इस्,
f. kind or good advice, salutary instruction, friendly
language.
—हितोपदेश (˚त-उप्˚), अस्, m. friendly
[]
advice, salutary instruction; N. of a celebrated and
very popular collection of stories and fables (supposed
to be narrated by a Brāhman named Viṣṇu-śarman
to some young princes, and intermixed with many
admirable didactic sentences and moral precepts ex-
tracted from various sources, the whole being chiefly
founded on the Pañca-tantra, q. v.: the stories illus-
trate four principal subjects, divided into four books,
viz. 1. Mitra-lābha, ‘the acquisition of friends;’
2. Suhṛd-bheda, ‘the separation of friends;’ 3. Vi-
graha, ‘war;’ 4. Sandhi, ‘peace;’ they have been
translated into nearly all the languages of Asia and
Europe, and have served as the substance of many
similar collections, such as the Anvāri Suhailī, Khirad-
afroz, Pilpay's Fables, &c.); N. of a work on medi-
cine; of another work on medicine by Śambhū-
nātha, (also called Vaidyaka-sāra-saṅgraha.)
—हितो-
पदेष्टृ (˚त-उप्˚), ता, m. a friendly instructor,
kind adviser.

हीत हीत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = हित (accord-
ing to some).

हितक, अस्, m. a child, the young of any animal,
a pupil, &c. (= शिशु, according to Śabda-k.).
